questions.question: Poisonous fumes can enter a cab because of:

options.text: Not enough oil in the engine.

questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system is dangerous. Poisonous fumes can leak into the cab or sleeper berth.

questions.question: When starting from a complete stop, a vehicle should:
questions.explanation: Your vehicle must not roll backwards when you start moving. This prevents hitting vehicles behind you.

questions.question: A safety valve opens at ____ pounds per square inch (psi).
questions.explanation: The safety valve stops too much air pressure from building up in the air brake system. It opens at 150 psi.

questions.question: If an air compressor has a belt, check it to make sure it is:
questions.explanation: Check the air compressor belt before each drive. Make sure it is tight and in good condition.

questions.question: You will be denied a HazMat endorsement if:

options.text: You are a resident of the state where you are applying.
You are seen as a security threat.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are seen as a security threat.
questions.explanation: You will be denied a HazMat endorsement if you give up U.S. citizenship, are not a lawful permanent resident, have certain felony convictions, have been judged mentally defective, were committed to a mental institution, or the TSA considers you a security threat.

questions.question: On a slippery surface, stopping distance:

options.text: Is longer than on dry pavement.
Is shorter than on dry pavement.
Is about the same as on dry pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is longer than on dry pavement.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance increases on slippery surfaces because your tires have less grip.

questions.question: If you have more than one license:

options.text: States share information, so you may get caught.

questions.correctAnswerText: States share information, so you may get caught.
questions.explanation: All states share driver information through a computer database to prevent people from having multiple licenses. It is illegal to have more than one driver license.

questions.question: While driving, ____ holds spring brakes in place.
questions.explanation: Air pressure holds spring brakes in place while driving. When air pressure drops low enough, the springs activate the brakes.

questions.question: At 55 mph on dry pavement, how many feet does brake lag add to your stopping distance?
questions.explanation: Stopping distance has four parts: perception distance, reaction distance, brake lag distance, and braking distance. At 55 mph on dry pavement with air brakes, brake lag adds about 32 feet to your total stopping distance.

questions.question: When exiting a vehicle, a driver should:

options.text: Keep at least one hand on the vehicle.

questions.explanation: When exiting your vehicle, face the vehicle and keep three points of contact at all times. For buses, hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly may cause you to fail the basic vehicle control skills test.

questions.question: Is driving at night safer or more dangerous than driving during the day?

options.text: Safer than driving during the day.
Just as safe as driving during the day.
More dangerous than driving during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous than driving during the day.
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous because it is harder to see hazards in the dark.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT an acceptable way to get CDL training?

options.text: Completing a certified course from an approved commercial driver training school
Completing a course of commercial driver training as required by an employer
Reading the official commercial driver's manual

questions.correctAnswerText: Reading the official commercial driver's manual
questions.explanation: To get a CDL for the first time, or if you have not had a commercial license in the past year, you must complete a training program from a state-approved school or registered employer.

questions.question: If your wheels spin when you accelerate on a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Take your foot off the accelerator.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the accelerator.
questions.explanation: If your wheels begin to spin while accelerating on a slippery surface, release the accelerator.

questions.question: When visibility is poor and other vehicles are near, what lights should you use?
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when traveling near other drivers in poor visibility, such as at dawn, dusk, or in bad weather. High beams can make it hard for other drivers to see.

questions.question: A 40-foot load must be secured with at least how many tie-downs?
questions.explanation: Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. All cargo must have at least two tie-downs, regardless of size.

questions.question: What should you do if mirrors are dirty before starting a trip?

options.text: They will likely become clean after driving a short distance.
It should not be a concern.
They should be cleaned before the vehicle is driven.

questions.correctAnswerText: They should be cleaned before the vehicle is driven.
questions.explanation: Before starting a trip, check your mirrors and windshield for dirt or anything that could block your vision. Clean them if needed.

questions.question: While driving, what should a driver watch?

options.text: Not be concerned with what is happening on the sides of their vehicle.
Be concerned with what is happening on all sides of the vehicle.
Not be concerned with what is happening behind the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be concerned with what is happening on all sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Always be aware of what is happening on all sides of your vehicle. Check the road ahead and use your mirrors regularly while driving.

questions.question: When must you tell your employer about a traffic violation conviction?
questions.explanation: You must tell your employer about any traffic violation conviction within 30 days. You must also tell your licensing agency within 30 days if the violation happened in another state. Parking tickets do not count.

questions.question: Transporting hanging meat in a refrigerated truck requires what kind of driver?

options.text: Is a good way for inexperienced drivers to gain experience.

questions.explanation: A skilled driver is needed because hanging meat is unstable. It has a high center of gravity and swings, which affects how the vehicle handles.

questions.question: Is emergency equipment required in vehicles?

options.text: Only required for vehicles that are transporting hazardous materials.

questions.explanation: Emergency equipment is required. During a pre-trip inspection, check for spare fuses, three red reflective triangles (or six fuses or three flares), and at least one fully charged fire extinguisher.

questions.question: A driver can start a new seven or eight day duty period after:
questions.explanation: In Washington State, a commercial driver must take at least 34 consecutive hours off before starting a new seven or eight day duty period.

questions.question: Brake linings should be:
questions.explanation: Brake linings must be free of oil and grease. They should not be loose or worn too thin.

questions.question: When parallel parking on the driver's side, you should:

options.text: Drive straight into the parking space.
Back past the parking space, then drive forward into it.
Drive past the parking space, then back into it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive past the parking space, then back into it.
questions.explanation: Drive past the parking space first. Then back up into it, getting the rear of your vehicle as close to the rear of the space as possible. Your vehicle must be completely within the space boundaries.

questions.question: Truck tractors with air brakes made on or after March 1, 1997 must have:
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes made on or after March 1, 1997 must have anti-lock brakes.

questions.question: When going down a steep hill, you should:

options.text: Use a low gear and engine braking.
Downshift instead of using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use a low gear and engine braking.
questions.explanation: On steep hills, use engine braking as your main way to control speed. Use the brakes only as backup.

questions.question: Before a trip, if you see fresh oil under your vehicle, this is:
questions.explanation: Fresh oil, coolant, grease, or fuel leaks under your vehicle are a cause for concern and should be checked before driving.

questions.question: Hydroplaning usually happens:

options.text: Where water collects on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where water collects on the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens where water has collected on the road. It can occur at speeds as low as 30 mph. Under-inflated or worn tires make hydroplaning more likely.

questions.question: If a vehicle's Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) breaks down:

options.text: The vehicle will have no brakes.
The vehicle will still have brakes.
The vehicle will go faster than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle will still have brakes.
questions.explanation: ABS only helps prevent wheel lockup. If it breaks down, the basic braking system still works. Drive and brake normally.

questions.question: What happens if air pressure gets too low in an air brake system?

options.text: The brakes may be slow to respond.

questions.explanation: If air pressure gets too low, the air brakes may stop working. This can happen if the compressor cannot replace the air lost from pressing the brake pedal.

questions.question: During the driving test, the examiner will score you on:
questions.explanation: The examiner will score you on driving maneuvers and your general driving behavior. You must drive safely, obey all traffic laws, and avoid accidents and violations.

questions.question: On a slippery road, a driver should:

options.text: Make turns as quickly as possible.

questions.explanation: On slippery roads, drive slowly and smoothly. Make gentle turns and avoid passing other vehicles.

questions.question: If you meet an aggressive driver, you should:

options.text: Try to stay in their way.

questions.explanation: When facing an aggressive driver, stay out of their way if you can. Do not make eye contact. Ignore any gestures they make.

questions.question: If a police officer asks you to take a blood alcohol test:

options.text: You can refuse with no penalty.
You can refuse but must pay a $50 fine.
You will lose your CDL if you refuse.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will lose your CDL if you refuse.
questions.explanation: Most states have Implied Consent Laws. By driving on public roads, you agree to take a drug or alcohol test if a police officer asks. If you refuse, you will lose your driving privileges. Know the laws in every state where you drive.

questions.question: When leaving a vehicle, you must keep ____ points of contact with the vehicle at all times.
questions.explanation: Face the vehicle as you exit and keep three points of contact at all times. On a bus, use the handrail. Exiting incorrectly can cause automatic failure on the basic control skills test.

questions.question: An encroachment occurs when:

options.text: A driver misses their basic skills test.
A vehicle touches a boundary line during the basic skills test.
A driver fails one section of the basic skills test.

questions.correctAnswerText: A vehicle touches a boundary line during the basic skills test.
questions.explanation: An encroachment happens when your vehicle touches or crosses a boundary line during a basic skills test exercise. Each encroachment counts as an error.

questions.question: Which is NOT a reason to cover cargo?

options.text: To protect people from spilled cargo

questions.explanation: Cover your cargo to protect people if it spills and to protect the cargo from weather.

questions.question: Skids from over-acceleration are usually fixed by:
questions.explanation: Release the accelerator to fix a skid caused by over-acceleration. This type of skid happens most often on snow or ice.

questions.question: When asked to change lanes during the driving test, you should:

options.text: Signal and change lanes when it is safe.
Change lanes quickly, even if it means cutting off another driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and change lanes when it is safe.
questions.explanation: During the driving test, check traffic and use your turn signal before changing lanes. Only change lanes when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: A commercial vehicle must:

options.text: Not have a fire extinguisher unless carrying hazardous materials.
Not have a fire extinguisher unless traveling through remote areas.
Have a fire extinguisher and other emergency equipment.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a fire extinguisher and other emergency equipment.
questions.explanation: All commercial vehicles must have proper emergency equipment. This includes spare fuses, three red reflective triangles or flares, and at least one fire extinguisher that is properly charged and rated.

questions.question: When hauling logs, a ____ light must be placed on the farthest point of the load.
questions.explanation: When hauling poles or logs, place a red light at the farthest point of the load. This light must be visible from the back and both sides.

questions.question: What is a Class 1 hazardous material?
questions.explanation: Class 1 hazardous materials are explosives. This includes items like ammunition, dynamite, and fireworks.

questions.question: If your driving test route does not include a railroad crossing, what might happen?

options.text: You will not have to do anything related to a crossing
You may have to explain how you would cross railroad tracks
You will have to take the test again on a route with a railroad crossing

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have to explain how you would cross railroad tracks
questions.explanation: If your driving test route does not include a railroad crossing, the examiner may ask you to explain and show how you would properly cross railroad tracks at a practice location.

questions.question: What is a wig wag?

options.text: A tube that carries air to the brakes
A type of air brake system

questions.explanation: A wig wag is a low air pressure warning device. It drops a mechanical arm into your view if the air pressure in the tanks drops below 55 to 75 psi. All vehicles with air brakes must have this device.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks?

options.text: Get out of the vehicle and call for help
Keep trying to get your vehicle off the tracks

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of the vehicle and call for help
questions.explanation: If your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, leave immediately and get away from the tracks. Look at the signposts at the crossing for emergency contact information and call 911 or another emergency number.

questions.question: If your personal vehicle license is revoked or suspended, can you get a hardship license for a commercial vehicle?

options.text: Yes, you can get a hardship license
No, you cannot get a hardship license
Your CDL will not be affected

questions.correctAnswerText: No, you cannot get a hardship license
questions.explanation: If your personal vehicle license is revoked, canceled, or suspended, you cannot get a hardship license to operate a commercial vehicle.

questions.question: When you start an engine, how long does it take for oil pressure to reach normal?
questions.explanation: Check your gauges when you start the engine. Oil pressure should reach normal within seconds after the engine starts.

questions.question: How should you complete an offset back-right parking maneuver?

options.text: Pull straight forward, then drive straight back
Drive straight back, then pull forward to the left
Pull straight forward, then back to the right

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull straight forward, then back to the right
questions.explanation: For an offset back-right parking maneuver, first pull straight forward, then back up to the right. Your vehicle must stay completely within the parking space boundaries.

questions.question: What should happen between dual tires?

options.text: They should always touch each other
They should not touch each other

questions.correctAnswerText: They should not touch each other
questions.explanation: When inspecting your vehicle, make sure dual tires do not touch each other or any other part of the vehicle.

questions.question: Which is not a recommended way to spot vehicle problems?

options.text: Checking critical items only at the start and end of a trip

questions.correctAnswerText: Checking critical items only at the start and end of a trip
questions.explanation: During a trip, check your vehicle often. Look at your gauges, mirrors, tires, cargo, and lights. Use all your senses to watch for any early signs of trouble.

questions.question: Where are braking mechanisms located?
questions.explanation: Drum brakes are attached to the wheels on the axles. The parts that make the vehicle stop are located inside the brake drum.
